sentences.text: The largest species, G. giganteus, stood about 2.15 meters tall and weighed between 175 and 225 kilograms.
The skull of G. giganteus was huge relative to its body and powerfully built.
The beak of G. giganteus was extremely tall and compressed from side to side.
Huge eggshell fragments were found in Late Paleocene deposits in Spain and early Eocene deposits in France.
A single isolated feather found in the Green River Formation resembles the broad, vaned body feathers of flighted birds.
The largest known Gastornis footprint impression measured 40 cm in length and tracks dated to about 53.7 million years old suggest they were made by Gastornis.
The genus Gastornis was first described in 1855 based on a fragmentary skeleton.
In 2020, a distinct species named G. laurenti was described based on specimens found near Saint-Papoul, southwestern France, making it the most recently described species of Gastornis.
Gastornis giganteus, formerly known as Diatryma gigantea, dates from the middle Eocene of western North America.
Evidence such as the absence of hooked claws and bone isotopic signatures suggests Gastornis was likely herbivorous, feeding on tough plants and seeds.
Gastornis species have traditionally been considered predators of small mammals, the most famous of which is the primitive horse Eohippus.
Gastornis is generally classified as related to the Galloanserae, which includes modern waterfowl and gamebirds.
It is generally accepted that there are at least five valid species of Gastornis.
The earliest Gastornis fossils come from Europe, suggesting the genus likely originated there.

It is debated whether Diatryma is a junior synonym of Gastornis or a distinct valid genus, because scientists debate the synonymy of Gastornis and Diatryma because detailed comparisons of type specimens have not yet been completed.
Louchart et al. (2021) argued that there is no unambiguous evidence to support the synonymy of Omorhamphus storchii with Gastornis giganteus due to a lack of definitive juvenile specimens.
The reason for the extinction of Gastornis is currently unclear.
